purpose: voice-split feasibility test — can Suno render N designated distinct voices in separated roles (duet / triple / quartet)?
variable_under_test: number of designated distinct voices (2/3/4) and whether they render as audibly separable
controls: same song concept '네 차례야', same hype/encouragement theme, full instrumental backing allowed (a-cappella purity NOT required)
difficulty_ladder: duet (male x female, easy baseline) -> triple (3 female) -> quartet (4 female, target case)
encoding_method: (1) SP defines each voice timbre by register+delivery; (2) per-section bracket role tags grounded in Suno corpus vocab (e.g. 'female vocals enter', 'female rap vocals'); (3) () inline vocal directives (corpus + Leo-verified)
listen_for: 각 지정 보이스가 음색으로 구별되는가 (뭉개지지 않는가)
랩 역할이 실제 랩으로, 메인이 멜로디로 분리 렌더되는가
동성(올-여성) 보컬일수록 분리가 무너지는 지점이 어디인가 (a<b<c 난이도)
지정 안 한 5번째 목소리가 끼어들지 않는가

songs.title: 네 차례야 (Duet)

voices.desc: bright clear young female, light head voice
warm husky male baritone, soft chesty tone

songs.hypothesis: male x female timbre contrast should separate cleanly — establishes baseline that designation works at all
songs.style_prompt: K-pop duet, mid-tempo emotional pop with full instrumental backing — piano, warm synth pad, soft 808 and clap beat. 92 BPM, key of C major. Two clearly distinct lead voices that alternate and stay identifiable, blending only in the chorus: Voice 1 is a bright, clear young female with a light head voice; Voice 2 is a warm, husky male baritone with a soft chesty tone. Verses trade line by line in a call-and-response format — the female sings a line, the male answers. The pre-chorus stacks the two in close two-part harmony. The final chorus opens in unison then splits into a third-apart harmony. Keep the two timbres separated and identifiable throughout — do not merge them into one voice. Korean lyrics, intimate and encouraging mood, late-night phone-call warmth.
songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
[Verse 1: bright female vocals]
(female) 새벽 두 시 너의 목소리
잠긴 듯 낮게 떨려
[Verse 1 answer: warm male vocals enter]
(male) 괜찮아 다 지나갈 거야
내가 여기 있잖아
[Pre-Chorus: female and male close two-part harmony]
한 줄씩 주고받은 말이
어느새 노래가 돼
[Chorus: both voices, unison then third-apart harmony]
네 차례야 이제 네 차례야
무대 위 조명은 너를 기다려
(female lead) 높이 (male harmony) 더 높이
같이 부르면 안 무서워
[Verse 2: warm male vocals]
(male) 떨리는 손 내가 잡을게
박자 놓쳐도 괜찮아
[Verse 2 answer: bright female vocals enter]
(female) 그럼 너도 같이 틀려줘
우리 둘이면 괜찮아
[Bridge: call and response]
(call: male) 준비됐어?
(response: female) 준비됐어
(both) 하나 둘 셋
[Final Chorus: both voices, third-apart harmony]
네 차례야 이제 우리 차례야
무대 위 조명은 우릴 기다려
(unison) 같이 같이
끝까지 같이 부르자
[Outro]

songs.title: 네 차례야 (Triple)
songs.hypothesis: same-sex 3-voice with one rap role — tests whether register+delivery alone separates without the male/female crutch
songs.style_prompt: K-pop girl-group track, three distinct female voices, energetic pop with full instrumental backing — bright synth, punchy 808, snappy clap beat. 100 BPM, key of A minor. Three clearly separable female timbres that must stay identifiable: Voice 1 is a bright, high belting lead carrying the main melody; Voice 2 is a husky, low chest-voice female who raps with a rhythmic spoken-flow; Voice 3 is an airy, breathy mid-range female for the hook and ad-libs. Verse 1 is sung by Voice 1; Verse 2 is rapped by Voice 2; the hook is led by Voice 3 with the others stacking three-part harmony. The bridge is a call-and-response between the rapper and the main. Keep the three voices distinct by pitch register and delivery — do not blend them into a single choir. Korean lyrics, confident hype-each-other-up mood.

songs.title: 네 차례야 (Quartet)
songs.hypothesis: target case — 4 same-sex voices. Highest blend risk; if this separates, full girl-group role-casting is viable
songs.style_prompt: K-pop girl-group anthem, four distinct female voices, high-energy pop with full instrumental backing — bright synths, heavy 808, festival clap beat. 105 BPM, key of B-flat major. Four clearly separable female timbres, each identifiable by register and delivery: Voice 1 bright high belting soprano (main melody); Voice 2 husky low chest-voice alto (rap, rhythmic spoken-flow); Voice 3 airy breathy mid-range (hook lead and ad-libs); Voice 4 warm round lower-mid (harmony anchor, lowest sung part). Verse 1 sung by V1; Verse 2 rapped by V2; the pre-chorus trades V3 and V1 line by line; the hook is led by V3 over a four-part female harmony stack with V1 on top and V4 on the bottom. The bridge is a four-way call-and-response, each voice entering one at a time. Keep all four distinct — do not collapse them into a unison choir. Korean lyrics, empowering girl-group hype mood.
